title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 678-680 of the 'suite à la Longue Marche'). Let 𝔊 be a discrete group with a family of subgroups M_i of finite index. These are commutative and finitely generated as ℤ-modules, so torsion-free ones are free of finite rank. They can be taken normal, since H-stable ones are cofinal (previous page). For each i there is an exact sequence of group schemes over S_0 (= Spec ℤ) of the form 1 → M̲_i → 𝔈_i → H_{S_0} → 1 (eq. 41), with H the finite quotient made constant. Here M̲_i is a group scheme attached to the lattice M_i. Its precise definition is on an earlier page; it is plausibly a pushout or 'algebraisation' of the lattice. For M_j ⊂ M_i, M̲_i is an extension of the constant finite group (M_i/M_j)_{S_0} by M̲_j. Hence M̲_i is a finite disjoint union of translates of M̲_j.

This page finishes the proof that the transition morphisms 𝔈_j → 𝔈_i are affine. The question being local, it reduces to the homomorphism E(M_i,M_j) → E(M_i,M_i). The source is affine as a finite sum of affine schemes, the target is affine, so the morphism is affine. Since transitions are affine, the projective limit of the 𝔈_i exists in the category of schemes (the limit functor is representable, EGA IV §8). This yields a group scheme over S_0 which is not of finite type.

Remark: the pro-group (𝔈_i) over S_0 depends only on two data:
- the discrete group 𝔊;
- a commensurability class of subgroups, assuming the class contains finitely generated ℤ-modules (free of finite type once small enough).
If the M_i have finite index in 𝔊, the class is canonical. The next page concludes that the pro-object depends only on 𝔊, provided 𝔊 has a finite-index subgroup that is commutative and finitely generated, i.e. is virtually ℤ^n ('virtabélien').

The next page names this Env(𝔊), a pro-system of affine group schemes over S_0 indexed by normal torsion-free abelian subgroups. It is functorial, compatible with products (47), and exact on short exact sequences of virtabelian groups (48-49).

Purpose: an 'algebraic envelope' over ℤ of virtually abelian discrete groups, crystallographic-type groups such as orbifold fundamental groups of genus-one or toroidal pieces. In Longue Marche-type Galois-Teichmüller considerations it presumably serves to compare discrete groups with their algebraic or profinite incarnations.
errors: No real error on this page. The affineness argument is correct: a finite disjoint union of affine schemes is affine, and a morphism between affine schemes is affine. Limits of projective systems with affine transition morphisms exist (EGA IV 8.2).
Gap: the definition of M̲_i is not on this page. Exactness of the limit and the claim that it is a group scheme are asserted ('pas difficile'), not proved.
Phrasing slip: 'si M est d'indice fini ... i.e. si M∩M_i finis' is muddled. The intended condition is that 𝔊/M_i be finite.

ideas.what: Projective limit of a pro-system of group schemes with affine transition maps is representable by a (non-finite-type) group scheme
ideas.modern_name: Limits of affine morphisms / pro-algebraic group schemes

ideas.what: Envelope Env(𝔊) of a virtually-ℤ^n discrete group as a pro-affine group scheme over Spec ℤ. It is built from extensions of the constant finite quotient by a group scheme attached to the lattice, depends only on the commensurability class of the lattice, and is functorial, multiplicative and exact.
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic hull / pro-algebraic (relative) completion of virtually polycyclic groups, here over ℤ
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mostow (algebraic hull of polycyclic groups, ca. 1970); Raghunathan; Hain (relative completion, 1990s); Malcev completion
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the Longue Marche to my knowledge; unsure

ideas.what: Data of a discrete group plus a commensurability class of finite-index abelian subgroups as the input of the construction; the term 'virtabélien'

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches an integral (over Spec ℤ) envelope functor Env from virtually abelian discrete groups to pro-affine group schemes. It is claimed to be exact and multiplicative and to depend only on the commensurability class of a lattice. Existing hull/completion theories (Mostow, Hain) work over fields, mostly ℚ or char 0. An integral version with constant finite parts and exactness over ℤ is not, to my knowledge, systematically developed.
missed.quote: la limite projective des 𝔊_i dans la catégorie des schémas existe ... avec un schéma en groupes — pas de t.f.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral models of completions of fundamental groups are of current interest (integral/p-adic Malcev and relative completions, integral homotopy types). A ℤ-envelope for crystallographic and orbifold groups could serve integral Galois-Teichmüller questions.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine affineness and limit-existence argument. It belongs to an unpublished construction of an integral pro-algebraic envelope of virtually abelian groups, which is mildly interesting but close to known algebraic-hull ideas.
transcription_corrections: 'sur S = Spec [?] 𝔊' should likely read 'sur S_0 = Spec ℤ'.

'il n'est pas difficile [?] de prouver que la limite cherchée, et la trouvaille [?] avec un schéma en groupes' probably reads 'que la limite cherchée est représentable par un schéma en groupes' or 'qu'on la trouve être un schéma en groupes'.
'(et la propriété est petite [?], il sera libre de t.f.)' likely '(et si M est assez petit, il sera libre de t.f.)'.
'Si M est d'indice [?] d'indice fini' is a repeated-word slip: 'Si M est d'indice fini dans 𝔊'.
In the margin, 'E(M_i,M_j) → E(M_i,M_i)' (previous page) is the morphism whose source and target are referred to as 'le premier' and 'le deuxième' here.
